description: Ground truth for the #14 cross-repo measurement (PRD §17 item 3). Every relation is known by construction: 'link' rows are real cross-repo relationships in the fixtures, 'no-link' rows are deliberate traps (near-misses that must NOT be linked). 'type' is the CBM edge type; 'async' matches CROSS_ASYNC_CALLS or CROSS_CHANNEL (CBM uses both for topic-style links); the pair {a,b} is unordered (edge direction is a CBM implementation detail the measurement does not presume); 'key' is the concrete route path or topic/channel name that must equal the edge detail (url_path/channel_name) — without it, two different transports between the same repo pair (kafka topic vs EventEmitter channel) would satisfy each other's relations. Constraints discovered while building the fixtures (verified against upstream pass_cross_repo.c) are noted inline — they are part of the measurement result, not fixture quirks.

relations.detail: GET /orders via fetch('/orders') -> express app.get('/orders', listOrders)
POST /payments via axios baseURL http://orders-api:3000 (axios instance method form). NOTE: axios instance methods (ordersApi.post) are not extracted in 0.10.8 — expected to miss as an extractor gap.
POST /payments via axios.post full URL -> app.post('/payments', chargePayment); url_path arrives as the full URL, so the key matches on the parsed pathname

fetch('/inline-orders') -> app.get('/inline-orders', async (req,res) => ...). Deliberate miss: the handler is an inline arrow function, and HANDLES is only emitted for identifier/string handler arguments (extract_calls.c: extract_handler_arg) — measures the miss side of the named-handler constraint rather than leaving it source-verified only.

kafkajs topic orders.created: producer.send in orders-api, consumer.subscribe in web-bff. NOTE: kafkajs produced no ASYNC_CALLS edges in 0.10.8 — the miss, if it occurs, is an extractor gap, not a matcher miss.

EventEmitter 'order.created': bus.emit in orders-api, bus.on with named handler in web-bff — the channel transport CBM documents for JS (LISTENS_ON requires a named handler, like HANDLES). The key distinguishes this channel from the kafka topic orders.created on the same repo pair.

OrderService.GetOrder: proto + grpc-js server in orders-api, client call in web-bff. NOTE: pass_cross_repo.c has no gRPC phase — the counter exists but no matcher runs; expected to miss as unimplemented upstream.
Query.order: schema + resolver in orders-api, @apollo/client gql query in web-bff. NOTE: same as gRPC — no GraphQL phase in pass_cross_repo.c; expected to miss as unimplemented upstream.
URLs appear only in constants/comments, never fetched
orders.created.v2 is a different topic than orders.created
payments.settled consumer has no producer anywhere
